25          Plaintiffs Cassandra Edwards, Allan Amsel, and Brittany Frank (“Plaintiffs”) respectfully

26   request that the Court enter the attached proposed order enabling third-party subpoena

27   respondent Verizon Wireless (“Verizon”) to produce certain customer records, and show the

28   Court as follows:
      Case 5:24-cv-05795-NW           Document 99        Filed 06/26/26      Page 2 of 5



 1   1. Plaintiffs served a subpoena dated April 20, 2026, requesting information from

 2      Verizon, including information relating to customer equipment and transactions. A

 3      true and correct copy of the document subpoena served on Verizon (“Subpoena”) is

 4      attached hereto as Exhibit A.

 5   2. Non-Party Verizon is compiling information responsive to the Subpoena and is

 6      prepared to produce it (subject to the terms and protections of the protective order

 7      entered in this case) after this Court enters an Order pursuant to California Public

 8      Utilities Code (“CPUC”) § 2894, finding good cause for the production of such

 9      information sought in the Subpoena and requiring Verizon to turn over the requested

10      information.

11   3. Plaintiffs believe such good cause exists under CPUC § 2894 because the requested

12      records are relevant to the claims and defenses in this litigation and subject to

13      disclosure upon court order. See Martin v. Global Tel*Link Corp.¸ 2017 U.S. Dist.

14      LEXIS 225617, at *6 (C.D. Cal. Dec. 6, 2017); see also Hoagland v. Axos Bank,

15      2021 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 221542, at *2 (S.D. Cal. Nov. 16, 2021) (“California law

16      permits the production of subscriber information pursuant to a court order.”). Verizon

17      is prepared to produce responsive information pursuant to such an order.

18   4. Under California law, telecommunications carriers are prohibited from disclosing

19      customer-identifying information absent express customer consent or a court order.

20      CPUC §§ 2891 and 2894. Section 2894 provides a limited exception that permits such
21      disclosure upon a court finding of good cause.
22   5. Plaintiffs seek data from Verizon relevant to the claims in this case, and all
23      disclosures will be subject to a protective order. Verizon is subject to the disclosure
24      restrictions and protections under the CPUC.
25   6. Verizon agrees to produce information or records responsive to the Subpoena during

26      the relevant time period to the extent Verizon is able to locate such information or

27      records subject to any objections, and provided that the Court enters an order enabling

28

 1      such production pursuant to the CPUC, including an order enabling production of

 2      IMEI data directly to Apple Inc.

 3   7. Verizon and Defendants have expressly authorized Plaintiffs to state that this motion

 4      is unopposed.

 5   8. Accordingly, Plaintiffs respectfully request that the Court enter the proposed order

 6      attached hereto.

 1          Pursuant to Civil Local Rule 6-2 and 7-12 and the Court’s April 2, 2026 Order, see Dkt. 85,

 2   Plaintiffs Cassandra Edwards, Allan Amsel, and Brittany Frank (“Plaintiffs”) and Defendants Apple

 3   Inc. and AppleCare Service Company, Inc. (collectively, “Apple” and together with Plaintiffs, the

 4   “Parties”), by and through their respective counsel of record, hereby stipulate to, and respectfully

 5   request, a stay of all case deadlines to allow the Parties to engage in settlement discussions and pursue

 6   private mediation. 1
 7          WHEREAS, Plaintiff Cassandra Edwards filed her initial Complaint on August 23, 2024;

 8          WHEREAS, Plaintiff Everett Scott filed his initial Complaint on September 30, 2024;

 9          WHEREAS, on October 29, 2024, the Court entered an order relating and consolidating
10   Edwards’s and Scott’s cases, and ordering Plaintiffs to file a Consolidated Amended Class Action

11   Complaint (“CAC”) by November 15, 2024;

12          WHEREAS, Plaintiffs filed the CAC on November 15, 2024, which added additional named

13   Plaintiffs Brittany Frank and Allan Amsel;

14          WHEREAS, Apple filed a motion to dismiss the CAC on December 13, 2024, and filed a related

15   motion to stay discovery pending resolution of Apple’s motion to dismiss on June 11, 2025;

16          WHEREAS, on July 31, 2025, the Court granted in part and denied in part Apple’s motion to

17   dismiss the CAC and denied Apple’s motion to stay discovery;

18          WHEREAS, the Parties exchanged Initial Disclosures on August 7, 2025;

19          WHEREAS, on October 24, 2025, the Court entered an order setting the operative case

20   schedule, under which the Parties’ next case deadline is the close of fact discovery on July 24, 2026;

21          WHEREAS, the Parties have been actively engaged in fact discovery—including production of

22   documents and responses to written discovery requests, as well as third party discovery—since the

23   exchange of Initial Disclosures on August 7, 2025, and, prior to that, Plaintiffs’ service of written

24   discovery requests on May 28, 2025;

25          WHEREAS, the Parties recently agreed to engage in private mediation, and on March 30, 2026,

26   filed an initial Joint Stipulation and [Proposed] Order for Stay of Case Deadlines to allow the Parties

27

28   1 Counsel for the Parties understand that Plaintiff Scott will be voluntarily dismissing his claims
     pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 41.

 1   to focus their efforts on the process of selecting a mutually agreeable mediator; scheduling a mediation

 2   session; and gathering information required to inform the Parties’ positions as to a fair and reasonable

 3   settlement of this action;

 4          WHEREAS, on April 2, 2026, the Court held a Case Management Conference to discuss the

 5   timing of mediation and effect of a stay on the case schedule and denied the Parties’ initial Joint

 6   Stipulation “without prejudice to renew provided the Parties addressed the concerns the Court

 7   expressed on the record on April 2, 2026 in any renewed stipulation,” Dkt. 85, including the objectives

 8   of having this case ready for trial by August 2027, three years after filing, and a class certification

 9   deadline of late summer 2026, Tr. at 4–5; 14;

10          WHEREAS, on April 8, 2026, the Parties met and conferred to discuss the Court’s concerns

11   and come to agreement on the timing of mediation, tasks to be completed ahead of mediation, the

12   litigation schedule should mediation not be successful, and a renewed Joint Stipulation;

13          WHEREAS, Plaintiffs’ putative class is defined as “All individuals who traded in or returned a

14   Covered Device under an AppleCare+ contract in the last four years whose contract was not

15   immediately cancelled, resulting in continuing subscription fees and/or a failure to provide prorated

16   refunds,” Dkt. 26 ¶ 69;

17          WHEREAS, the Parties agree that for purposes of mediation, it is necessary to prioritize the

18   collection and exchange of (1) Apple internal data reflecting the refunds that Apple has already

19   provided to putative class members who traded in or returned Covered Devices directly to Apple and

20   continued to be charged for AppleCare+ coverage and/or did not receive prorated refunds for unused

21   coverage; (2) third-party data that may allow the Parties to identify putative class members who traded

22   in or returned Covered Devices to an Apple Authorized Reseller and continued to be charged for

23   AppleCare+ coverage and/or did not receive prorated refunds for unused coverage; and (3) Apple

24   internal data that may serve as a proxy for estimating the scope of the putative class of customers who

25   traded in or returned Covered Devices to an Apple Authorized Reseller and continued to be charged

26   for AppleCare+ coverage and/or did not receive prorated refunds for unused coverage, to the extent

27   third-party data is not available;

28          WHEREAS, Apple is in the process of collecting the data described in (1) and (3) above, which


                                                        2
     No. 5:24-cv-05795-NW                                                    JOINT STIPULATION AND [PROPOSED]
                                                                            ORDER FOR STAY OF CASE DEADLINES
           Case 5:24-cv-05795-NW            Document 91         Filed 04/21/26       Page 4 of 7



 1   requires coordination with multiple internal teams and collection from multiple data sources, and the

 2   Parties are working cooperatively to prepare and serve subpoenas, building on prior subpoenas to and

 3   responses from pertinent third-parties, requesting the third-party data described in (2) above;

 4           WHEREAS, the parties anticipate finalizing and serving the subpoenas described above by

 5   April 20, 2026;

 6           WHEREAS, based on prior subpoena responses, the Parties anticipate that it may take weeks if

 7   not months to collect and have experts analyze available third-party data described in (2) above;

 8           WHEREAS, the materials and efforts described above are also important to preparing this case

 9   for trial, should the Parties be unable to resolve this matter at mediation;

10           WHEREAS, the Parties agree that while an understanding of Plaintiffs’ arguments in support

11   of class certification would inform the Parties’ settlement positions, it is not necessary for Plaintiffs to

12   file their class certification motion, or for the Parties to fully brief that motion, in advance of mediation;

13   instead, Plaintiffs will share their anticipated class certification brief and pertinent expert report with

14   Apple pursuant to Rule 408;

15           WHEREAS, the Parties agree that they will continue to advance focused discovery efforts

16   beyond the items above ahead of mediation such that they can promptly proceed with custodial and

17   further ESI discovery and deposition discovery to ensure that this matter is ready for trial by August

18   2027 should mediation not succeed;

19           WHEREAS, the Parties agree that an August mediation strikes an appropriate balance between

20   allowing the Parties time to focus their efforts on prioritizing the ongoing collection, exchange, and

21   analysis of the third-party and Apple-internal data to inform their positions on a fair and reasonable

22   settlement, while also allowing for a modified case schedule, as proposed below, that would

23   accommodate a trial by the end of the summer of 2027, should mediation be unsuccessful;

24           WHEREAS, the Parties have now scheduled mediation with a mutually agreeable private

25   mediator for August 28, 2026;

26           NOW THEREFORE, the Parties hereby stipulate and agree as follows:

27

28

 1           1.     This action shall be stayed through September 4, 2026, one week after the parties’

 2   participation in private mediation; provided, however, that the parties retain the right to conduct

 3   discovery reasonably necessary to inform mediation including the use of third-party subpoenas;

 4           2.     Apple will prioritize collection and production of the Apple internal data required to

 5   inform the Parties’ settlement positions by May 29, 2026, subject to any unavoidable delays that may

 6   arise in the collection and production process, while endeavoring to make rolling productions to the

 7   extent possible ahead of said date;

 8           3.     To further inform the Parties’ settlement positions, Plaintiffs will provide Apple with

 9   their anticipated motion for class certification by May 29, 2026;

10           4.     The Parties will submit a joint status report on or before June 5, 2026 to inform the

11   Court of the status of pre-mediation data collection and production, including the status of the Parties’

12   third-party subpoena requests;

13           5.     After completion of the priority items above within the Parties’ control, the Parties will

14   negotiate and agree to custodians, search terms, search locations, and other items related to the scope

15   of the custodial and further ESI review and production that the Parties will undertake should mediation

16   be unsuccessful, but the Parties will not move forward with such ESI review and production, or

17   depositions, during the stay;

18           6.     The Parties will submit a further joint status report on or before September 4, 2026,

19   informing the Court of the status of their efforts to resolve this action through mediation and, if

20   mediation is unsuccessful, proposing an updated case schedule with an August 2027 trial date.

21   Assuming an August 23, 2027, trial date consistent with the Court’s comments at the April 2, 2026,

22   case management conference (i.e., three years after the original Complaint was filed) and subject to the

23   Court’s consideration and approval, the Parties anticipate proposing a schedule tracking the dates

24   outlined below, should mediation be unsuccessful:

25      •    September 11, 2026: Class Certification Deadline;
26      •    February 12, 2027: Fact Discovery Deadline;
27      •    February 26, 2027: Opening Expert Reports;
28      •    March 19, 2027: Rebuttal Expert Reports;

 2         Having considered the Parties’ stipulation, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED THAT:

 3          1.      This action shall be stayed, and all case deadlines shall be held in abeyance, through

 4   September 4, 2026; provided, however, that the Parties retain the right to conduct discovery reasonably

 5   necessary to informed mediation including the use of third-party subpoenas;
